title: Race-free writes with ON CONFLICT and RETURNING
problem: Implement three writes for the messenger without the read-then-write pattern: joining a chat (report whether it was new), recording a read marker that never moves backwards, and deleting a chat's messages while reporting which ids were deleted.
requirements: join_chat returns True when the membership was added and False when it already existed, using a single INSERT and no SELECT
mark_read creates the marker or moves it forward, never backwards, and returns the stored value
mark_read writes with one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT statement
delete_chat_messages deletes the chat's messages in one DELETE ... RETURNING statement and returns their ids in ascending order
contract: join_chat(conn, chat_id, user_id) -> bool; mark_read(conn, chat_id, user_id, message_id) -> int; delete_chat_messages(conn, chat_id) -> list[int]
expectedBehavior: mark_read(conn, 1, 10, 9) == 9, then mark_read(conn, 1, 10, 4) == 9; join_chat(conn, 1, 10) is True, then False
edgeCases: Markers for other chats or users are separate
Deleting from a chat with no messages
RETURNING rows come back in arbitrary order
hints: Conceptual: let the uniqueness constraint decide what happens on a duplicate, and let RETURNING tell you what happened, instead of asking with a SELECT first.

Specific: DO NOTHING plus RETURNING gives no row when nothing was inserted. In DO UPDATE, excluded.col is the value you tried to insert and table.col is the stored one; SQLite's max(a, b) picks the larger.

Implementation: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (chat_id, user_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING chat_id, then `fetchone() is not None`. For mark_read: DO UPDATE SET last_read_id = max(read_markers.last_read_id, excluded.last_read_id) RETURNING last_read_id. For the delete: sorted(row[0] for row in rows).
evaluation: You can say what RETURNING returns for DO NOTHING on a conflict
